separable: inseparable — the object follows *on*: *gaining on us*, never ✗ *gain us on*.
gloss: To get closer to someone or something ahead of you.
examples: That blue car has been *gaining on* us since the last exit.
She *gained on* the leader with every lap.
By mile ten he had *gained on* the whole front pack.

ru: ополчаться, ополчиться (на кого-л.); наваливаться всем вместе
separable: inseparable — the target comes after *on*: *they ganged up on him*, never ✗ *they ganged him up on*. Without a target it stands alone: *they all ganged up*.
gloss: To join with others against one person.
examples: Don't all *gang up on* me at once.
The other kids *ganged up on* him at recess.
Three networks are *ganging up on* the same story.

separable: separable — *gas up the car* or *gas the car up*, and with a pronoun it must split: *gas it up*. Just as often there is no object at all: *we stopped to gas up*.
transitivity: both — transitive (gas up the truck), intransitive (stop and gas up)
gloss: To fill a vehicle's tank with gasoline.
examples: I need to *gas up* before we get on the highway.
He *gassed up* the truck at the station on Route 9.
We're *gassing up* and then heading straight out.
contrast: *Gas* doubles the s: *gassed*, *gassing*. The third-person form is usually written *gasses*, though *gases up* also appears.

separable: separable — *gather up the toys*, *gather the toys up*, and with a pronoun *gather them up*.
gloss: To collect scattered things quickly into one armful or pile.
examples: *Gather up* your things — the bus leaves in five minutes.
She *gathered up* the papers that had blown off the desk.
He was *gathering* the kids' shoes *up* by the door.

separable: usually no object — the thing you are getting ready for arrives through *for*: *gear up for the season*. When it does take an object it separates: *gear the plant up for production*, *gear it up*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (gear up for the holidays), transitive (gear the factory up)
gloss: To get ready for something big or demanding that is coming.
examples: Stores *gear up* for the holidays right after Halloween.
The team *geared up* for a long playoff run.
We've been *gearing up* for this inspection all month.

ru: ориентировать, сориентировать (на кого-л.); рассчитывать (на определённую публику)
separable: the object always sits between the two parts — *gear the class toward beginners*, *gear it toward beginners*; ✗ *gear toward beginners the class*. Learners meet it most often in the passive: *the course is geared toward beginners*.
gloss: To design or aim something at a particular group or purpose.
examples: They *geared* the whole class *toward* absolute beginners.
These ads are *geared toward* buyers under thirty.
We're *gearing* the campaign *toward* first-time voters.
contrast: American English writes *toward*; *towards* is the British form. *Gear to* (*geared to a younger audience*) means the same thing.

separable: inseparable — *glance over the contract*, never ✗ *glance the contract over*. (The separable one is *look it over*.)
gloss: To read something quickly without studying it.
examples: Could you *glance over* this email before I send it?
She *glanced over* the menu and ordered the usual.
He's *glancing over* the numbers now and will call back.

separable: inseparable — *glance through the report*, never ✗ *glance the report through*.
gloss: To look quickly through the pages of something, stopping nowhere long.
examples: I *glanced through* the report on the plane.
He *glances through* the paper while the coffee brews.
She was *glancing through* a magazine in the waiting room.

separable: no object — intransitive. The subject is the eyes, or the person behind them: *his eyes glazed over*, *the whole room glazed over*.
gloss: Of the eyes, to lose focus because the person has stopped taking anything in.
examples: His eyes *glazed over* halfway through the presentation.
Mention the tax code and everybody *glazes over*.
I could see the students *glazing over*, so I stopped.

separable: inseparable — *gloss over the problem*, never ✗ *gloss the problem over*.
gloss: To mention something so briefly that its worst or hardest parts get no attention.
examples: The report *glosses over* the safety violations.
He *glossed over* the part where he lost the money.
She's been *glossing over* how hard that first year was.

separable: inseparable — *the doubt gnawed at her*, never ✗ *gnawed her at*. Often stretched for emphasis: *gnaw away at*.
gloss: Of a worry, doubt, or guilt, to keep troubling someone for a long time.
examples: The mistake *gnawed at* her for months.
Something about his story keeps *gnawing at* me.
Guilt had been *gnawing at* him since March.
contrast: The *g* is silent: *gnaw* is /nɔː/, like *naw*. Forms are regular — *gnaws*, *gnawed*, *gnawing*.

separable: separable — *gobble up the last slice*, *gobble the last slice up*, *gobble it up*.
gloss: To eat something very fast and finish all of it.
examples: The kids *gobbled up* every last cookie.
He *gobbles up* whatever's left in the pan.
She's *gobbling* it *up* like she hasn't eaten in days.

separable: separable — *gobble up the competition*, *gobble them up*.
gloss: To buy up, take over, or use up something completely and fast.
examples: A bigger chain *gobbled up* the family stores one by one.
Rent *gobbles up* half her paycheck.
Developers are *gobbling up* the farmland east of town.

separable: separable — *gobble down breakfast*, *gobble your dinner down*, *gobble it down*.
gloss: To swallow food quickly, almost without chewing.
examples: He *gobbled down* a sandwich and ran for the bus.
Don't *gobble* your dinner *down* like that.
They were *gobbling down* pancakes when I got there.

separable: no object — intransitive: *quit goofing around*. A companion arrives through *with*: *goofing around with his cousins*.
gloss: To play and act silly instead of being serious.
examples: Quit *goofing around* and finish your homework.
We *goofed around* in the parking lot for an hour.
He *goofs around* in class and then wonders why he's failing.

separable: no object — intransitive: *he goofs off all day*.
gloss: To avoid the work you are supposed to be doing and waste time instead.
examples: He *goofs off* all afternoon and then stays late to catch up.
They *goofed off* the entire week the boss was away.
I've been *goofing off* instead of studying for the test.
contrast: *Goof off* is avoiding work; *goof around* is fooling around; *goof up* is making a mistake. Same verb, three different particles, three meanings.

separable: separable when there is an object — *goof up the order*, *goof the order up*, *goof it up*. Very often used with no object at all: *I goofed up*.
transitivity: both — transitive (goof up the order), intransitive (sorry, I goofed up)
gloss: To make a careless mistake, or to spoil something by making one.
examples: Sorry — I *goofed up* the order.
Everybody *goofs up* the first few times.
He keeps *goofing up* the easy ones and getting the hard ones right.

separable: inseparable — *grapple with the problem*, never ✗ *grapple the problem with*.
gloss: To struggle hard to understand or deal with something difficult.
examples: The city is still *grappling with* its housing shortage.
She *grappled with* the decision for weeks.
We have *grappled with* this same question all year.

separable: inseparable — *gravitate toward the back row*, never ✗ *gravitate the back row toward*.
gloss: To be drawn to a person, place, or kind of thing again and again.
examples: New students *gravitate toward* the loudest table in the room.
He *gravitated toward* jobs where nobody looked over his shoulder.
Buyers have been *gravitating toward* smaller cars all year.
contrast: American English writes *toward*, British *towards*; *gravitate to* is equally good.

separable: inseparable — *it grates on me*, never ✗ *it grates me on*. Often with *nerves*: *grate on my nerves*.
gloss: To irritate someone steadily, a little more with every repetition.
examples: His laugh really *grates on* me.
The music *grated on* my nerves after the first hour.
Her constant corrections were *grating on* everyone at the table.

ru: вызывать отвращение, вызвать отвращение; противно кому-л.
separable: separable — *gross out the whole table* or *gross the whole table out*, and with a pronoun it **must** split: *it grossed me out*, never ✗ *it grossed out me*.
gloss: To disgust someone.
examples: That story totally *grossed* me *out*.
He *grosses out* his little sister on purpose.
The smell in the fridge was *grossing* everybody *out*.

ru: остерегаться, остеречься; принимать меры против, предотвращать
separable: inseparable — *guard against infection*, never ✗ *guard infection against*.
gloss: To act in advance so that something bad does not happen.
examples: Wash your hands to *guard against* infection.
The rule was written to *guard against* exactly this situation.
We're *guarding against* a repeat of last winter.

separable: separable — *gulp down the medicine*, *gulp your coffee down*, *gulp it down*.
gloss: To swallow a drink or food quickly, in big mouthfuls.
examples: He *gulped down* a glass of water and kept running.
She *gulps* her coffee *down* on the way out the door.
They were *gulping down* soda between innings.

ru: забивать, забить (механизм); засорять, засорить; портить дело
separable: separable — *gum up the works*, *gum the machine up*, *gum it up*. Common in the passive: *the printer got gummed up*.
gloss: To clog something with something sticky, or to make a smooth process stop running.
examples: Sap had *gummed up* the saw blade.
One missing signature can *gum up* the whole process.
You're *gumming up* the works with all these extra forms.
contrast: *Gum* doubles the m: *gummed*, *gumming*. *Gum up the works* is the fixed phrase Americans reach for most.

separable: separable — *gun down the suspect*, *gun him down*. Most often heard in the passive: *he was gunned down*.
gloss: To shoot someone, usually killing them, when they cannot defend themselves.
examples: Two officers were *gunned down* in the street.
The robber *gunned down* a guard and ran.
In the opening scene he *guns down* a witness in broad daylight.

separable: inseparable — *gunning for the top job*, never ✗ *gun the job for*.
gloss: To be openly and hard at work trying to get something.
examples: She's *gunning for* the manager's job and everybody knows it.
He *gunned for* a starting spot all season.
Both teams are *gunning for* first place this weekend.

ru: ополчиться (на кого-л.); точить зуб, охотиться за кем-л.
separable: inseparable — *gunning for him*, never ✗ *gun him for*.
gloss: To be looking for a chance to attack, blame, or get rid of a particular person.
examples: The new boss has been *gunning for* him since day one.
Reporters *gunned for* the mayor after the memo leaked.
Watch what you say in there — they're *gunning for* you.

separable: inseparable — *gush over the baby*, never ✗ *gush the baby over*. *Gush about* works the same way.
gloss: To praise someone or something in an excited, exaggerated way.
examples: Everyone *gushed over* the baby for twenty minutes.
She *gushes over* every picture he posts.
They were still *gushing over* the new kitchen when we left.
